<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>BMW Product Strategy AI</title>

  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Saira+Condensed:wght@400;600;700;800&family=Saira+Semi+Condensed:wght@300;400;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/reveal.js@5.1.0/dist/reset.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/reveal.js@5.1.0/dist/reveal.css">

  <style>
    :root {
      /* Keynote ground + tints (sampled from BMW PM keynote) */
      --night: #0a1726;
      --petrol: #035970;
      --ice: #c3e7f0;
      --mist: #c8d7e0;
      --steel: #85acb9;
      --slate: #548d9e;
      --white: #ffffff;
      --line: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92);
      --line-soft: rgba(200, 215, 224, 0.28);
      --veil: rgba(8, 20, 34, 0.38);

      /* BMW corporate */
      --bmw-blue: #1c69d4;
      --bmw-blue-active: #0653b6;
      --m-red: #e22718;
      --rose: #ffb3ab;
      --amber: #f2c46d;

      --display: 'Saira Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;
      --text: 'Saira Semi Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;
      --ease: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
    }

    html, body, body.reveal-viewport {
      background: var(--night);
      color: var(--white);
      font-family: var(--text);
      -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
    }
    ::selection { background: var(--bmw-blue); color: var(--white); }

    /* ---------- Keynote ground ---------- */
    #ground {
      position: fixed; inset: -6%;
      z-index: 0;
      background: url('assets/keynote-ground.webp') center / cover no-repeat;
      animation: groundDrift 48s ease-in-out infinite alternate;
      pointer-events: none;
    }
    #ground::after {
      content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0;
      background: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 120%, rgba(3, 89, 112, 0.35), transparent 60%);
    }
    @keyframes groundDrift {
      from { transform: scale(1) translate3d(0, 0, 0); }
      to   { transform: scale(1.08) translate3d(-2%, 1.5%, 0); }
    }

    .reveal { z-index: 1; font-family: var(--text); color: var(--white); }
    .reveal .slides { text-align: left; }
    .reveal .progress { display: none; }
    .reveal .controls { color: var(--mist); }
    .reveal .slides section { height: 720px; padding: 0; }

    /* Fragments: exponential ease-out from an already-composed layout */
    .reveal .fragment { transition: opacity 0.7s var(--ease), transform 0.7s var(--ease), filter 0.7s var(--ease), visibility 0.7s; }
    .reveal .fragment.rise { transform: translateY(14px); filter: blur(4px); }
    .reveal .fragment.rise.visible { transform: none; filter: none; }

    /* ---------- Type ---------- */
    .h-display {
      margin: 0;
      font-family: var(--display);
      font-weight: 700;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      line-height: 0.95;
      letter-spacing: 0;
      color: var(--white);
    }
    .h-slide { font-size: 46px; }
    .lede { font-weight: 300; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--mist); margin: 10px 0 0; max-width: 62ch; }
    .label {
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase;
      color: var(--steel);
    }
    .num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

    /* ---------- Glyphs ---------- */
    .glyph { width: 22px; height: 22px; flex: none; fill: currentColor; color: var(--mist); }
    .glyph.sm { width: 18px; height: 18px; }
    .ico { width: 18px; height: 18px; flex: none; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: square; stroke-linejoin: miter; }
    .authors { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; color: var(--mist); }

    /* ---------- Hairline box grammar (keynote "The Process") ---------- */
    .box { border: 1.5px solid var(--line); position: relative; }
    .box-soft { border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); }

    /* ---------- Slide frame ---------- */
    .frame { position: absolute; inset: 0; padding: 40px 56px 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    .frame-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 32px; min-height: 76px; }
    .context { display: flex; gap: 0; }
    .context span {
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; text-transform: uppercase;
      padding: 7px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); color: var(--mist);
      margin-left: -1px;
    }
    .frame-body { flex: 1; min-height: 0; padding-top: 22px; position: relative; }

    /* ---------- Process rail (signature) ---------- */
    .rail { height: 78px; padding-top: 18px; flex: none; }
    .rail ol { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr); margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    .rail li {
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 1.4px; text-transform: uppercase;
      color: rgba(200, 215, 224, 0.38);
      transition: color 0.6s var(--ease);
    }
    .rail li.done { color: var(--steel); }
    .rail li.on { color: var(--white); }
    .rail-line { position: relative; height: 2px; margin-top: 10px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); }
    .rail-line::after {
      content: ''; position: absolute; right: -2px; top: -5px;
      border-left: 9px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); border-top: 6px solid transparent; border-bottom: 6px solid transparent;
    }
    .rail-progress { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--white); }
    .rail-head { position: absolute; top: -4px; width: 10px; height: 10px; background: var(--white); margin-left: -5px; }

    /* ---------- Buttons (BMW corporate, 0 radius) ---------- */
    .btn {
      display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px;
      height: 48px; padding: 0 28px;
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; text-transform: uppercase;
      background: var(--bmw-blue); color: var(--white);
      border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer;
      transition: background-color 0.25s var(--ease), transform 0.25s var(--ease);
    }
    .btn:hover { background: #2a78e4; }
    .btn:active { background: var(--bmw-blue-active); transform: translateY(1px); }
    .btn:focus-visible, .tile:focus-visible, .act:focus-visible, .mic:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ice); outline-offset: 3px; }

    /* =========================================================
       0 · TITLE
       ========================================================= */
    .title-car {
      position: absolute; right: -150px; top: 40px; width: 1010px; height: 674px;
      background: url('assets/concept-car.webp') center / cover no-repeat;
      -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, #000 26%, #000 100%), linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0%, #000 14%);
      -webkit-mask-composite: source-in; mask-composite: intersect;
      mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, #000 26%, #000 100%), linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0%, #000 14%);
    }
    .title-copy { position: absolute; left: 56px; top: 150px; width: 640px; }
    .title-copy h1 { font-size: 96px; line-height: 0.9; }
    .title-copy .sub { margin-top: 26px; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--mist); max-width: 30ch; }
    .title-arrow { position: absolute; left: 56px; right: 56px; bottom: 96px; height: 2px; background: var(--white); transform-origin: left; }
    .title-arrow::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: -2px; top: -5px; border-left: 10px solid var(--white); border-top: 6px solid transparent; border-bottom: 6px solid transparent; }
    .title-meta { position: absolute; left: 56px; bottom: 52px; }
    .title-meta strong { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .title-meta span { display: block; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 300; color: var(--steel); margin-top: 2px; }
    .car-credit { position: absolute; right: 56px; bottom: 52px; text-align: right; }
    .car-credit strong { display: block; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; }
    .car-credit span { font-family: var(--display); font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; color: var(--steel); }

    /* =========================================================
       1 · PROBLEM
       ========================================================= */
    .problem { position: absolute; inset: 0; padding: 56px; }
    .problem h2 { font-size: 64px; }
    .quote-col { position: absolute; left: 56px; top: 210px; width: 600px; padding-left: 28px; border-left: 1.5px solid var(--line); }
    .quote-col blockquote {
      margin: 0; padding: 0; width: auto; background: none; box-shadow: none; font-style: normal;
      font-size: 34px; line-height: 1.28; font-weight: 300; color: var(--white);
    }
    .quote-col blockquote b { font-weight: 700; }
    .quote-col .who { margin-top: 26px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
    .quote-col .who strong { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .cloud { position: absolute; left: 720px; top: 150px; width: 520px; height: 470px; }
    .cloud span {
      position: absolute; white-space: nowrap;
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.6px;
      animation: float 14s ease-in-out infinite alternate;
    }
    @keyframes float { from { transform: translateY(0); } to { transform: translateY(-10px); } }
    .problem-foot { position: absolute; left: 56px; right: 56px; bottom: 52px; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; }
    .problem-foot strong { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 24px; }
    .problem-foot span { font-weight: 300; font-size: 16px; color: var(--steel); }

    /* =========================================================
       2 · SITUATION ANALYSIS
       ========================================================= */
    .setup { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 0; }
    .setup .group { padding: 18px 20px 20px; }
    .setup .group + .group { border-left: 0; }
    .group-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 14px; }
    .tiles { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; }
    .tile {
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 600; font-size: 17px; letter-spacing: 0.6px; text-transform: uppercase;
      padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); background: transparent; color: var(--mist);
      cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0;
      transition: border-color 0.25s var(--ease), background-color 0.25s var(--ease), color 0.25s var(--ease);
    }
    .tile:hover { border-color: var(--line); color: var(--white); }
    .tile.sel { border: 2px solid var(--white); padding: 8px 13px; color: var(--white); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08); }

    .sources { margin-top: 18px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr); }
    .source { padding: 16px 18px 18px; border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); margin-left: -1px; }
    .source h4 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 19px; text-transform: none; letter-spacing: 0; color: var(--white); }
    .source p { margin: 4px 0 12px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 300; color: var(--steel); }
    .weight { display: flex; gap: 3px; }
    .weight i { width: 12px; height: 6px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16); }
    .weight i.f { background: var(--ice); }
    .run { margin-top: 26px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 28px; }
    .run-log { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 300; color: var(--mist); }
    .run-log div { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
    .run-log b { font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); }

    /* =========================================================
       3–6 · REQUIREMENTS TABLE
       ========================================================= */
    .table { border-top: 1.5px solid var(--line); }
    .row {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 54px 300px 1fr 64px 128px;
      align-items: center; gap: 18px;
      height: 70px; padding: 0 14px 0 6px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft);
      background-color: rgba(8, 20, 34, 0);
      color: var(--white);
    }
    .rank { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 38px; line-height: 1; text-align: center; color: var(--white); }
    .req-name { position: relative; display: inline-block; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.1; }
    .req-grp { display: block; margin-top: 3px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 300; color: var(--steel); letter-spacing: 0.3px; }
    .why { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--mist); }
    .why b { font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); }
    .tag {
      display: inline-block; margin-right: 8px; padding: 2px 7px 1px;
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; text-transform: uppercase;
      vertical-align: 1px;
    }
    .tag.ev { color: #0a1726; background: var(--ice); }
    .tag.as { color: #2a1d05; background: var(--amber); }
    .tag.rj { color: var(--white); background: var(--m-red); }
    .tag.ai { color: var(--white); background: var(--bmw-blue); }
    .tag.gap { color: var(--ice); border: 1px solid var(--ice); padding: 1px 6px 0; }
    .actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 6px; position: relative; }
    .act {
      width: 36px; height: 36px; display: grid; place-items: center;
      border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); background: transparent; color: var(--mist); cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0;
      transition: border-color 0.2s var(--ease), color 0.2s var(--ease), background-color 0.2s var(--ease);
    }
    .act:hover { border-color: var(--line); color: var(--white); }
    .act.no:hover { border-color: var(--m-red); color: var(--m-red); }
    .act.pressed { background: var(--m-red); border-color: var(--m-red); color: var(--white); }

    .row.rejected { background-color: rgba(226, 39, 24, 0.16); color: var(--rose); }
    .row.rejected .rank, .row.rejected .req-name { color: var(--rose); }
    .strike { position: absolute; left: -3px; top: 50%; height: 2px; width: 0; background: var(--m-red); }
    .present .strike.draw { animation: strike 0.6s var(--ease) 0.6s forwards; }
    .strike.done { width: calc(100% + 6px); }
    @keyframes strike { to { width: calc(100% + 6px); } }
    .row.archived { height: 56px; opacity: 0.6; }

    .row.fresh { background-color: rgba(28, 105, 212, 0.26); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px #5b97ea; position: relative; overflow: hidden; }
    .row.fresh::after {
      content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: -30%; width: 30%;
      background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18), transparent);
      transform: skewX(-18deg);
    }
    .present .row.fresh { animation: slideIn 0.9s var(--ease) 0.35s backwards; }
    .present .row.fresh::after { animation: sweep 1.4s var(--ease) 1.1s; }
    @keyframes slideIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(90px); } }
    @keyframes sweep { to { left: 120%; } }
    .badge { display: inline-block; margin-left: 10px; padding: 3px 8px 2px; vertical-align: 3px; background: var(--bmw-blue); font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 1.4px; }
    .divider { padding: 14px 0 8px 6px; }

    .cursor { position: absolute; width: 24px; height: 24px; z-index: 5; pointer-events: none; filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55)); }
    .cursor.parked { right: 40px; bottom: -60px; opacity: 0; }
    .cursor.on { right: 6px; top: 20px; }
    .cursor .ring { position: absolute; left: -9px; top: -9px; width: 20px; height: 20px; border: 2px solid var(--m-red); border-radius: 50%; opacity: 0; }
    .present .cursor.on .ring { animation: ring 0.7s ease-out 0.55s; }
    @keyframes ring { 0% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(0.3); } 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2.2); } }

    .status { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 1.4px; text-transform: uppercase; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); color: var(--mist); }
    .status .pulse { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: var(--ice); animation: pulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; }
    .status.ok { border-color: var(--ice); color: var(--ice); }
    @keyframes pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.25; } 50% { opacity: 1; } }

    /* =========================================================
       4 · RED TEAM
       ========================================================= */
    .focus-row { border-top: 1.5px solid var(--line); border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--line); background-color: rgba(8, 20, 34, 0.35); }
    .debate { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; margin-top: 18px; }
    .side { padding: 16px 20px 18px; }
    .side + .side { border-left: 0; }
    .side-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding-bottom: 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft); margin-bottom: 4px; }
    .side-head h3 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 22px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: var(--white); }
    .side.against .side-head h3 { color: var(--rose); }
    .claim { padding: 11px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(200, 215, 224, 0.12); font-size: 16px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--mist); }
    .claim:last-child { border-bottom: 0; }
    .claim b { font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); }
    .claim q { display: block; margin-top: 4px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--steel); quotes: '\201C' '\201D'; }
    .verdict { margin-top: 16px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 22px; padding: 14px 20px; background: var(--white); color: var(--night); }
    .verdict .label { color: var(--petrol); }
    .verdict strong { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 800; font-size: 26px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .verdict span { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; color: #23384a; }
    .confidence { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
    .confidence .bars { display: flex; gap: 3px; }
    .confidence .bars i { width: 14px; height: 18px; background: rgba(10, 23, 38, 0.15); }
    .confidence .bars i.f { background: var(--m-red); }

    /* =========================================================
       7 · DECISION MEMORY
       ========================================================= */
    .memory { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 330px 1fr; height: 100%; max-height: 452px; }
    .capture { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 24px; }
    .capture + .ledger { border-left: 0; }
    .mic {
      width: 112px; height: 112px; border-radius: 50%; border: 0; cursor: pointer;
      display: grid; place-items: center; background: var(--bmw-blue); color: var(--white);
      position: relative; transition: background-color 0.4s var(--ease);
    }
    .mic .ico { width: 40px; height: 40px; stroke-width: 1.8; }
    .mic::before, .mic::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -14px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5); opacity: 0; }
    .listening .mic::before { animation: ripple 2s ease-out infinite; }
    .listening .mic::after { animation: ripple 2s ease-out 1s infinite; }
    @keyframes ripple { from { opacity: 0.9; transform: scale(0.85); } to { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1.5); } }
    .saved .mic { background: var(--white); color: var(--night); }
    .wave { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; height: 44px; }
    .wave i { width: 3px; height: 4px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3); }
    .listening .wave i { background: var(--white); animation: wave 0.85s ease-in-out infinite; }
    @keyframes wave { 50% { height: var(--h); } }
    .mic-state { height: 18px; }
    .mic-state span { display: none; }
    .memory-slide:not(.listening):not(.saved) .mic-state .idle,
    .listening .mic-state .rec,
    .saved .mic-state .done { display: inline; }
    .listening .mic-state .rec { color: var(--white); }
    .saved .mic-state .done { color: var(--ice); }

    .ledger { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    .entry-head { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 22px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft); }
    .entry-head .what { font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .entry-head .what .tag { vertical-align: 3px; }
    .entry-head .by { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--steel); }
    .transcript { flex: 1; padding: 20px 22px; font-size: 30px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 1.38; color: var(--white); }
    .transcript .mark { color: var(--steel); }
    .caret { display: inline-block; width: 2px; height: 1em; margin-left: 2px; vertical-align: -0.12em; background: var(--white); animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
    @keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }
    .saved .caret { display: none; }
    .spec { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); border-top: 1px solid var(--line-soft); }
    .spec div { padding: 14px 22px; opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); transition: opacity 0.6s var(--ease), transform 0.6s var(--ease); }
    .spec div + div { border-left: 1px solid var(--line-soft); }
    .spec strong { display: block; margin-top: 4px; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; color: var(--white); }
    .saved .spec div { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
    .saved .spec div:nth-child(2) { transition-delay: 0.12s; }
    .saved .spec div:nth-child(3) { transition-delay: 0.24s; }

    /* =========================================================
       8 · ONE CAR
       ========================================================= */
    .outcome { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 330px 1fr; height: 100%; }
    .approved { padding-top: 4px; }
    .approved li { list-style: none; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 22px 1fr; gap: 10px; align-items: start; padding: 10px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft); }
    .approved li .ico { color: var(--ice); margin-top: 3px; }
    .approved li strong { display: block; font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; }
    .approved li span { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 300; color: var(--steel); }
    .approved ul { margin: 10px 0 22px; padding: 0; }
    .stage { position: relative; margin-right: -56px; }
    .stage-car {
      position: absolute; inset: -40px 0 -10px -40px;
      background: url('assets/concept-car.webp') 60% 55% / cover no-repeat;
      -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, #000 18%);
      mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, #000 18%);
    }
    .hot { position: absolute; width: 0; height: 0; }
    .hot .dot { position: absolute; left: -5px; top: -5px; width: 10px; height: 10px; background: var(--white); outline: 4px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25); }
    .hot .lead { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1px; background: var(--white); transform-origin: top; }
    .hot .lab {
      position: absolute; white-space: nowrap; transform: translate(-50%, -100%);
      font-family: var(--display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; text-transform: uppercase;
      padding: 5px 10px; background: rgba(10, 23, 38, 0.82); border: 1px solid var(--line);
    }
    .hot .lab em { font-style: normal; color: var(--ice); margin-right: 6px; }
    .enter .hot .dot { animation: pop 0.5s var(--ease) backwards; }
    .enter .hot .lead { animation: grow 0.6s var(--ease) backwards; }
    .enter .hot .lab { animation: labIn 0.6s var(--ease) backwards; }
    .enter .hot:nth-of-type(1) * { animation-delay: 0.3s; }
    .enter .hot:nth-of-type(2) * { animation-delay: 0.45s; }
    .enter .hot:nth-of-type(3) * { animation-delay: 0.6s; }
    .enter .hot:nth-of-type(4) * { animation-delay: 0.75s; }
    .enter .hot:nth-of-type(5) * { animation-delay: 0.9s; }
    @keyframes pop { from { transform: scale(0); } }
    @keyframes grow { from { transform: scaleY(0); } }
    @keyframes labIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -80%); } }

    /* Entrance only when navigating forward */
    .enter .rise-in { animation: riseIn 0.9s var(--ease) backwards; }
    .enter .rise-in.d1 { animation-delay: 0.12s; }
    .enter .rise-in.d2 { animation-delay: 0.24s; }
    .enter .rise-in.d3 { animation-delay: 0.36s; }
    .enter .draw-in { animation: drawIn 1.4s var(--ease) 0.2s backwards; }
    @keyframes riseIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); filter: blur(6px); } }
    @keyframes drawIn { from { transform: scaleX(0); } }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; }
    }
  </style>
</head>

      <symbol id="i-mic" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M9 3h6v11H9zM5.5 11.5a6.5 6.5 0 0013 0M12 18v3M8.5 21h7"/></symbol>

    </defs>
  </svg>

  <div class="reveal">

      autoAnimateEasing: 'cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)',
    });

    // Entrance motion replays only when moving forward.
    function playEnter(slide) {
      slide.classList.remove('enter');
      void slide.offsetWidth;
      slide.classList.add('enter');
    }

    // Waveform
    const wave = document.getElementById('wave');
    for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
      const bar = document.createElement('i');
      bar.style.setProperty('--h', (8 + Math.round(Math.abs(Math.sin(i * 1.3) * Math.cos(i * 0.4)) * 36)) + 'px');
      bar.style.animationDelay = (i * 0.04) + 's';
      wave.appendChild(bar);
    }

    // Voice transcription
    const memory = document.getElementById('memory');
    const speech = document.getElementById('speech');
    const SPEECH = 'Rejecting the brakes because of supply-chain delays. The new aerodynamic requirement fits the sportiness focus better.';
    let timer = null;

    function startTyping() {
      stopTyping();
      memory.classList.add('listening');
      let i = 0;
      const tick = () => {
        i++;
        speech.textContent = SPEECH.slice(0, i);
        if (i < SPEECH.length) {
          const ch = SPEECH[i - 1];
          timer = setTimeout(tick, 22 + Math.random() * 30 + (ch === '.' ? 380 : ch === ' ' ? 40 : 0));
        } else {
          timer = setTimeout(() => {
            memory.classList.remove('listening');
            memory.classList.add('saved');
            speech.textContent = SPEECH + '”';
          }, 450);
        }
      };
      timer = setTimeout(tick, 800);
    }
    function stopTyping() {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      speech.textContent = '';
      memory.classList.remove('listening', 'saved');
    }
    memory.querySelector('.mic').addEventListener('click', startTyping);

    // Selectable tiles (objectives)
    document.querySelectorAll('.tiles').forEach(group => {
      group.addEventListener('click', e => {
        const tile = e.target.closest('.tile');
        if (!tile) return;
        group.querySelectorAll('.tile').forEach(t => t.classList.toggle('sel', t === tile));
      });
    });

    let last;
    function onSlide(current, previous, index) {
      if (previous && previous !== current) previous.classList.remove('enter');
      if (last === undefined || index > last) playEnter(current);
      if (current === memory) startTyping();
      else if (previous === memory) stopTyping();
      last = index;
    }
    Reveal.on('ready', e => onSlide(e.currentSlide, null, e.indexh));
    Reveal.on('slidechanged', e => onSlide(e.currentSlide, e.previousSlide, e.indexh));

# PM

A dependency-free prototype for turning automotive customer evidence into cited, context-sensitive requirements and preserving the reasoning behind each decision.

## Run

Requires Node.js 20+ and PowerShell 5+.

```powershell
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key'
# Optional; defaults to gpt-4o-mini
$env:OPENAI_MODEL='gpt-4o-mini'
node server.mjs
```

Open `http://localhost:4173`. Wait for the setup button to change from **Loading verified evidence…** to **Generate evidence-backed requirements** before continuing.

Do not launch `public/index.html` with a static-only preview server: stakeholder interpretation requires the Node API routes. If the header reports an outdated or missing PM API, stop the previous process with `Ctrl+C`, run `node server.mjs` again, and hard-refresh the browser.

The API key is read only by the Node server and is never returned to or stored by the browser. Do not place an API key in `public/`, source control, or browser `localStorage`.

To regenerate the normalized evidence file from the supplied archive:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\ingest-evidence.ps1
```

Run verification with:

```powershell
node --test
```

## Demonstration

1. Keep BMW 5 Series / G60 and United States selected.
2. Enter the target months, available people, and deadline importance.
3. Generate the requirements.
4. Select a feature group and open **Evidence & reasoning**.
5. Inspect the separate existence and ranking explanations and exact workbook-row citations.
6. Return to setup, change the deadline context, and regenerate to observe ranking changes.
7. Open **Check feasibility**, review the suggested owner and editable unsent email. You can dictate rough email notes and use **Create email from notes** without losing the default draft.
8. Paste `Feasible, but it requires an additional three months.`
9. Select **Process Feedback & Recalibrate**. Review the structured outcome, confidence, conditions, constraints, and timing.
10. Confirm the interpretation. Feasibility-only updates can recalibrate the group but are not written to **Decision memory**.
11. Select **Approve**. A decision note is optional; the approval and its supplied or default reason are stored for that exact vehicle and market.

Requirements are organized into four BMW vehicle domains: **Interior & Comfort**, **Exterior & Utility**, **Digital Experience & Controls**, and **Driving & Powertrain**. This keeps the review surface coherent while still ranking no more than ten requirements inside each domain.

Within those four stable navigation domains, PM derives evidence-based outcome clusters such as seating comfort, cargo access, connected access, parking confidence, and ride and handling. PMs can rename, split, merge, reorder, and move requirements without losing their citations.

## Grounding and provenance

`scripts/ingest-evidence.ps1` reads the supplied ZIP and `competitor_bmw_format.xlsx`. It creates `data/evidence.json` with exact filename, sheet, source row, original feedback ID, vehicle, market, classification, and original text. It also creates `data/context.json`, containing 1,003 customer-study rows, 12 sales-volume rows, 132 competitor signals, 13 competitor price references, source-file metadata, and verified PDF page counts. All nine supplied files are copied to `data/sources/` for direct inspection. The current generated feedback store contains 13,771 classification rows.

Frequency is calculated from unique feedback IDs within a feature, not spreadsheet rows. This prevents one comment assigned to several classifications from being presented as several customers. Low-quality and unclassified feedback remains in the evidence store but is excluded from requirements.

Requirement language, feature grouping, ownership routing, competitor-signal matching, and time-to-market fit are generated by deterministic, inspectable prototype logic. The application remains demonstrable without an API key. OpenAI-assisted email redrafting and stakeholder-response interpretation are disabled until the server key is configured.

## Current prototype boundaries

- Feedback, customer-study, sales-volume, original option-list, and competitor benchmark files are ingested. Ranked claims attach matching feedback, study, competitor, and vehicle/market sales records with workbook-row citations; competitor citations also link to the original external source recorded in the workbook.
- Original PDFs and verified page counts are available, but PDF text extraction is intentionally omitted because no reliable parser is installed. No PDF content or page citation is fabricated.
- Requirement grouping and planning estimates remain deterministic demo logic. Stakeholder-response interpretation and email drafting use the OpenAI Responses API. Competitor inputs come from the supplied, row-cited workbook rather than a separate market-intelligence tab.
- Only requirement approvals, approvals with conditions, and rejections containing a reason are exposed and appended as Decision Memory records. They are mirrored in browser storage; a production deployment should add authentication, signatures, backups, and formal retention controls.
- One approved record explicitly labeled **Team-authored demo history** seeds the memory experience. It is never presented as a verified BMW decision. The unresolved demo record is excluded from Decision Memory.
- Email is drafted only. The application does not send external messages.

## Architecture

- `scripts/ingest-evidence.ps1`: read-only archive ingestion and normalization
- `data/evidence.json`: generated evidence store with source lineage
- `src/engine.mjs`: grouping, deduplication, ranking, citations, and routing
- `src/openai.mjs`: stakeholder interpretation, grounded email drafting, and cited web research
- `public/`: application workflow and interface
- `server.mjs`: dependency-free static server
- `test/`: grounding and ranking invariants

The implementation is deliberately inspectable: deterministic frequency and ranking calculations are separated from natural-language explanations, and every displayed citation resolves to an ingested evidence record.

This prototype keeps those answers together instead of separating the requirement list from its evidence and decision history. ## End-to-end workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Customer feedback
studies, sales and competitors] --> B[Normalized evidence
with row-level provenance] B --> C[Vehicle and market filtering
deduplication and ranking] C --> D[Top requirements
in four vehicle domains] D --> E[PM review
citations and reasoning] E --> F[Stakeholder feasibility loop] F --> G[Approve or reject] G --> H[Decision memory
and audience-specific PDFs] ``` 1. **Define the product cycle.** Select a BMW vehicle, target market, time to market, available team, and deadline priority. 2. **Generate requirements.** The ranking engine filters evidence to the selected vehicle and market, removes low-quality input, deduplicates feedback frequency, and combines customer, study, sales, competitor, and delivery-context signals. 3. **Review the evidence.** Each requirement exposes separate explanations for why it exists and why it received its rank, plus exact source citations. 4. **Validate feasibility.** The application suggests a responsible department, prepares an editable email, and provides a Gmail compose link. It never sends the email. 5. **Process the response.** A pasted stakeholder reply can be interpreted as feasible, feasible with conditions, or not feasible. The PM must confirm the interpretation before it changes the requirement or ranking. 6. **Make the decision.** The PM can approve, approve with conditions, reject, or delete a requirement. Rejection recalibrates the affected group. 7. **Preserve and export.** Decision Memory records only approvals and rejections with their reasons. Structured PM, Technical, and GTM PDFs can then be generated. ## Main product areas ### Overview The landing page establishes the product context. The current evidence includes BMW 1 Series/F70, 5 Series/G60, and 7 Series/G70 material across the markets available for each vehicle. The PM controls: - vehicle and target market; - desired time to market; - available team size; - importance of protecting the deadline. Changing these inputs and regenerating the cycle can change requirement fit scores and ranking. ### Requirements Requirements are organized into no more than four stable BMW vehicle domains: - **Interior & Comfort** - **Digital Experience & Controls** - **Driving & Powertrain** - **Exterior & Utility** Each domain contains at most ten supported requirements; fewer are shown when the evidence does not justify ten. Requirements are not padded to reach a fixed count. Every requirement includes: - an atomic outcome statement; - its rank and priority score; - unique evidence frequency and market-signal count; - a suggested responsible entity; - a planning estimate, not an engineering feasibility claim; - “why this exists” and “why this rank” explanations; - citations resolving to the original workbook, sheet, and row; - approval, rejection, deletion, and feasibility actions. PMs can also rename, split, merge, and recalibrate groups, move requirements, and edit requirement wording without losing the source evidence. ### Decision Memory Decision Memory is intentionally narrow. It records only: - approved requirements; - requirements approved with conditions; - rejected requirements; - the PM-provided or generated reason for that decision. Searchable timeline entries preserve the requirement, actor, timestamp, decision, reason, and supporting evidence. Ordinary navigation, report generation, group edits, and feasibility-only updates are not added to Decision Memory. ### PDF reports The three exports serve different audiences: | Report | Contents | | --- | --- | | **PM PDF** | Every requirement, separated into its primary Technical or GTM audience, followed by the approval/rejection decision record. | | **Technical PDF** | Only requirements whose primary audience is engineering or technical delivery, including owner, status, evidence basis, representative sources, and routing rationale. | | **GTM PDF** | Only requirements whose primary audience is go-to-market, including customer evidence, market signals, representative sources, and routing rationale. | Technical and GTM assignments are mutually exclusive, so the two departmental reports are not duplicates. With OpenAI configured, a strict structured-output classification selects the primary audience. Without it, an inspectable deterministic classifier provides the fallback. The PM report always contains the complete requirement set. ## Evidence and traceability The checked-in normalized store was produced from the supplied archive and competitor workbook. The current fixture contains: - 13,771 feedback-classification rows; - 1,003 customer-study rows; - 12 sales-volume rows; - 132 competitor signals; - 13 competitor price references; - nine copied source files with source metadata; - three original PDFs with verified page counts. `data/evidence.json` retains the original filename, sheet, source row, feedback ID, vehicle, market, classification, quality, and text. `data/context.json` contains studies, sales planning, competitor evidence, source metadata, and PDF page-count metadata. Frequency is calculated from unique original feedback IDs within a feature—not raw spreadsheet rows—so one comment assigned to several classifications is not presented as several customers. Low-quality and unclassified feedback remains traceable in the evidence store but is excluded from generated requirements. The prototype does not extract claims from the supplied PDFs because a reliable PDF parser is not installed. It exposes the original files and verified page counts without fabricating PDF text or page citations. ## Deterministic logic and OpenAI responsibilities The system deliberately separates auditable calculation from language generation. ### Deterministic and inspectable - vehicle/market filtering; - feedback deduplication and quality exclusion; - evidence selection and citation validation; - BMW domain and outcome clustering; - frequency, market, sales, competitor, and delivery-context scoring; - ranking and the maximum of ten requirements per domain; - fallback requirement wording, ownership, email, and report routing. ### OpenAI-assisted when configured - rewriting requirement wording using only evidence attached to that requirement; - redrafting the stakeholder email from PM notes; - interpreting pasted stakeholder responses through a strict feasibility schema; - assigning each requirement to one primary Technical or GTM report audience. OpenAI cannot change the deterministic rank, feature, group, or selected evidence during requirement wording synthesis. Returned evidence IDs and claims are validated before the wording is accepted. Stakeholder interpretations never take effect until the PM confirms them. ## Running the application ### Prerequisites - Node.js 20.12 or newer - PowerShell 5 or newer only if you need to regenerate the evidence store - An OpenAI API key for the optional AI-assisted features There are no npm runtime dependencies to install. ### Start without OpenAI The core evidence, ranking, citations, approvals/rejections, default email draft, Gmail link, deterministic report routing, and PDF exports work without an API key. ```powershell npm start ``` Open [http://localhost:4173](http://localhost:4173). Wait for **Loading verified evidence…** to become **Generate requirements**. ### Start with OpenAI Recommended: use a `.env` file. The server loads it from the project root on start; it is gitignored. ```bash cp .env.example .env # then paste your key into OPENAI_API_KEY npm start ``` Variables already set in your shell take precedence over `.env`. Alternatively, set them directly. PowerShell: ```powershell $env:OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key' # Optional; defaults to gpt-4o-mini $env:OPENAI_MODEL='gpt-4o-mini' npm start ``` macOS or Linux: ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key' # Optional; defaults to gpt-4o-mini export OPENAI_MODEL='gpt-4o-mini' npm start ``` The API key is read only by the Node server. It is never returned to the browser or stored in browser local storage. Do not put keys in `public/`, committed files, or client-side code. Do not open `public/index.html` directly or use a static-only preview server. The browser needs the API and evidence routes served by `server.mjs`. If the header reports an outdated PM API, stop the previous process with `Ctrl+C`, restart `npm start`, and hard-refresh the page. ## Suggested first demonstration 1. Start the server and open the Overview tab. 2. Keep **BMW 5 Series · G60** and **United States** selected. 3. Use 18 months, 12 people, and deadline priority 8/10. 4. Generate the requirements and open one vehicle domain. 5. Expand **Evidence & reasoning** and inspect the existence explanation, ranking explanation, and exact citations. 6. Return to Overview, change the delivery context, and regenerate to see its effect on ranking. 7. Open **Check feasibility**, inspect the suggested department and editable email, then paste: `Feasible, but it requires an additional three months.` 8. Process and confirm the interpretation. 9. Approve or reject the requirement and inspect its Decision Memory entry. 10. Export the PM, Technical, and GTM PDFs and compare their scopes. ## Regenerating the evidence store The repository already includes normalized data, so this is optional. To ingest another archive and competitor workbook: ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\ingest-evidence.ps1 ` -Archive 'C:\path\to\source-archive.zip' ` -CompetitorWorkbook 'C:\path\to\competitor_bmw_format.xlsx' ` -Output 'data\evidence.json' ``` The script reads the source files, rebuilds the normalized evidence and context stores, and copies inspectable originals to `data/sources/`. It does not modify the source archive or workbook. ## Testing Run the complete test suite: ```powershell npm test ``` The tests cover source presence, ingestion integrity, deduplication, exact vehicle/market filtering, citations, domain limits, ranking sensitivity, competitor and market evidence, feasibility recalculation, approval/rejection behavior, decision-memory boundaries, strict OpenAI outputs, departmental routing, and PDF generation/pagination. ## Repository structure ```text public/ app.js Browser workflow and state management engine.js Deterministic requirement generation and ranking pdf-report.js Dependency-free structured PDF renderer index.html Application shell *.css / image assets BMW-inspired responsive interface src/ openai.mjs Server-side OpenAI integrations and validation report-routing.mjs Technical/GTM routing and deterministic fallback decision-memory.mjs Allowed decision-event types and reason handling engine.mjs Test/runtime re-export of the browser engine data/ evidence.json Normalized feedback evidence with provenance context.json Studies, sales, competitors, and source metadata decision-events.ndjson Append-only approval/rejection records historical-decisions.json Explicitly labeled demonstration history sources/ Original files available for inspection scripts/ ingest-evidence.ps1 Read-only source ingestion and normalization test/ Node test suite for product and audit invariants server.mjs Static file server plus server-side API routes docs/acceptance-audit.md Detailed implementation and prototype-boundary audit ``` ## Prototype boundaries - Planning estimates help rank work; they are not engineering feasibility conclusions. - Initial ownership suggestions are routing aids and remain PM-editable. - Speech transcription depends on browser support and always has a typed fallback. - The application drafts emails and Gmail compose links but never sends messages. - Decision events are appended to NDJSON and mirrored in browser storage. Production use would require authentication, durable actor identity, tamper-evident signatures, access controls, backups, and retention policies. - Competitor information used by the main requirement pipeline comes from the supplied, row-cited workbook. There is no separate Market Intelligence tab in the current interface. - Historical demo decisions are clearly labeled and must not be treated as verified organizational history. For a requirement-by-requirement implementation audit, see [`docs/acceptance-audit.md`](docs/acceptance-audit.md).

The README describes **BMW Product Intelligence**, a prototype that turns BMW customer feedback, studies, sales and competitor data into ranked requirements, each citing the spreadsheet rows it came from. It has no npm dependencies.

**Workflow (7 steps)**
1. **Set up the cycle:** the PM picks vehicle and market (1, 5 or 7 Series), then enters time to market, team size and how much the deadline matters.
2. **Generate:** the ranking engine filters to that vehicle and market, drops low-quality feedback, removes duplicates, and scores customer, study, sales, competitor and delivery signals.
3. **Review:** each requirement shows why it exists, why it has its rank, and citations down to workbook, sheet and row.
4. **Check feasibility:** the app suggests which department owns the requirement and drafts an editable email with a Gmail link. It never sends anything.
5. **Process the reply:** the PM pastes the stakeholder's answer, which is interpreted as feasible, feasible with conditions, or not feasible. Nothing changes until the PM confirms.
6. **Decide:** approve, approve with conditions, reject or delete. A rejection re-ranks that group.
7. **Record and export:** approvals and rejections go into Decision Memory, and the app exports three PDFs.

**Main areas**
- **Requirements:** four fixed domains (Interior & Comfort, Digital Experience & Controls, Driving & Powertrain, Exterior & Utility) with at most 10 requirements each. Lists are never padded. PMs can rename, split, merge and move requirements without losing citations.
- **Decision Memory:** stores only approvals and rejections with their reasons. Navigation, edits and feasibility-only updates are not logged.
- **PDF reports:** the PM report has everything, followed by the decision record. The Technical and GTM reports each contain only their own requirements, with no overlap.

**What's calculated vs. what the AI does**
- **Calculated by code:** filtering, de-duplication, scoring, ranking, citations, and the default wording and routing. All of this works without an API key.
- **OpenAI, only when a key is set:**
  - rewriting requirement wording from attached evidence only;
  - redrafting emails from PM notes;
  - interpreting stakeholder replies;
  - deciding whether each requirement goes to the Technical or GTM report.
- **Guardrail:** the AI cannot change ranks, groups or which evidence is selected, and its output is checked before use.

**Data**
- 13,771 feedback classification rows (all vehicles), 1,003 customer-study rows, 12 sales rows, 132 competitor signals and 13 competitor prices.
- Duplicates are counted by unique feedback ID, so one comment filed under several categories counts as one customer.
- The source PDFs are stored but their text isn't extracted, because no reliable PDF parser is installed.

**Running it:** Node 20.12+, then `npm start` and open http://localhost:4173, with the key in `.env` or the shell. The suggested demo is 5 Series G60, United States, 18 months, 12 people, deadline 8/10, with the reply "Feasible, but it requires an additional three months." Run the tests with `npm test`.

**Stated limits:** planning estimates are not engineering judgments; emails are drafted, not sent; Decision Memory has no authentication or tamper-proof signing; voice input depends on browser support; and there is no separate market-intelligence tab.

**Mismatches between the app and the pitch deck:**
- **The red-team feature doesn't exist in the app.** There's no "challenge" or devil's-advocate code anywhere, yet the deck has a whole slide for it. If a judge asks to see it live, there's nothing to show.
- **Group names differ.** The deck shows an "Exterior & dynamics" group, while the app's four domains split that across Exterior & Utility and Driving & Powertrain.
- **Recalibration is triggered differently.** In the deck, a supply-chain rejection swaps in a new requirement. In the app, recalibration comes from the feasibility reply or a rejection.

Either the deck should match the app, or the red-team feature needs to be built. Which do you want?

You don't need to hard-code anything. The real ranking for your demo setup (5 Series G60, US, 18 months, 12 people, deadline 8/10) already contains the bad example you're looking for, on the same screen as the good one.

**What the app actually ranks in "Driving & Powertrain":**

| Rank | Requirement | Score | Unique feedback | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | Drivetrain response | 91 | 315 | high |
| #10 | WiFi hotspot | 51 | 8 | medium |

The scores split like this:
- **Drivetrain (91):** genuinely earned. It has the most feedback of anything, full market evidence, and fits the schedule.
- **WiFi hotspot (51):** customer demand contributes only about 1 point. Roughly 41 points come from "quick to build" (15 months, fits the 18-month target) and 9 from market signals. It's on the list because it's cheap, not because customers want it.

That's your honest negative case, and it's real. Other domains show the same pattern: in Digital, #10 is traffic camera info (6 records, medium confidence); in Exterior, #2 has more feedback than #1 but ranks lower because it takes 24 months.

**Why I'd avoid hard-coding a fake critical reason:**
- Your pitch is "it doesn't make up reasons". If the honest-sounding weak reason is scripted and a judge clicks a different requirement in Q&A, or asks how it decided, you're stuck.
- A #10 that is truly bad would also look like a ranking bug. A borderline #10 that the tool openly flags as borderline is far more believable.

**How to frame it on stage:**
1. Open the domain and show #1: "315 customers, high confidence, here are the rows."
2. Scroll to #10 on the same screen: "Same tool, same rules. It tells us this one is weak: 8 customers, and nearly all its score comes from being quick to build. It's a candidate for cutting, and it says so itself."
3. Optionally, change the deadline priority and regenerate. The weak items move while the strong ones hold, which shows the ranking really responds to the PM's settings.

**The gap to fix:** the app's current "why this rank" text is a mechanical number dump ("Feedback frequency: 8 (3/100)… fit 100/100…"). A judge won't read that as the AI saying "this is weak". I'd add a short caveat line, generated from the same numbers, so it can't be made up. For example:

> "Weak customer signal: 8 records. Most of its score comes from fast delivery, not demand. Validate before committing."

It would appear automatically whenever demand is a small share of the score or confidence isn't high. It only triggers from real data, so it's honest by construction, and the same rule would also show the opposite on #1 ("Strong signal: 315 records").

**One thing a judge might notice:** WiFi hotspot sits under "Driving & Powertrain" because the domain sorting falls back to that group for features it doesn't recognize. Either fix the domain rules (hotspot belongs in Digital Experience) or demo with Digital's #10 (traffic camera info) instead.

content.text:
The app now shows plain-language reasons, an honest caveat on weak requirements, readable citations, and bigger text for the projector. All 37 tests pass, and I checked the result in Chrome at 1440 and 1280 px wide. Nothing is committed yet.

**Weak and strong signal:** each requirement now gets a colour-coded label based on how many customers raised it: Strong (100+), Solid (25–99), Limited (10–24) or Weak (under 10). Weak and Limited ones also show an **Honest caveat** box, built from the same numbers that produced the ranking. The demo pair, both in Driving & Powertrain (5 Series G60, US, 18 months, 12 people, deadline 8/10):
- **#1 Drivetrain, 91/100, Strong:** 315 customers raised it, and customer demand is the biggest part of its score.
- **#10 High-voltage charging socket, 51/100, Weak:** "Only 5 customers raised this. Just 1 of its 51 points comes from customer demand; the rest is timeline fit (41) and market evidence (9). Validate demand before committing."

**Domain fix:** WiFi hotspot, eSIM, USB, radio, voice assistant, vehicle key and driver profile now go to Digital Experience & Controls. Glove box, A/C and headrest go to Interior, and windows, wipers and frunk to Exterior. That's why Driving's #10 changed from WiFi hotspot to the charging socket.

**Reasoning panel**, used both on the card and in the side panel:
- **Two short bullet lists:** "Why it exists" and "Why rank #N", e.g. "Fits the 18-month target", "Tied on score with X, which more customers raised".
- **Score breakdown:** a bar showing what makes up the score (customer demand, timeline fit, market evidence), with no normalisation maths.

**Citations:** grouped by source:
- **Groups:** What customers said, Customer study, Competitors, Sales planning.
- **Quote first:** the quote leads, with a short source line underneath ("G60 customer feedback · row 394") that still opens the original file.
- **Long text collapsed:** very long texts like the Mercedes incident report are cut short with "Read full text", and only 4 citations show per group before "Show N more".

**Bug fixed:** the card's "Priority" number was actually showing the timeline-fit score, which is why so many requirements read "100/100". It now shows the real priority score.

content.text:
The "Responsible department" text box is now a dropdown labelled "Send this question to". Each requirement's most likely department is pre-selected and marked "· suggested", and the email draft rewrites itself when you pick another department. All 38 tests pass, and I tested it in the browser by opening Drivetrain and rerouting it to Purchasing & Cost Controlling.

**How it worked before:** the department came from just 5 keyword rules, and 53 of 120 requirements fell back to "Product Integration", including Drivetrain, Braking and cruise control. Some matches were wrong: "4WD/AWD" went to Software because "applicable" contains "app", and wireless phone charging went to E-Mobility. The draft was the same text every time; only the department name changed.

**How it works now:**
- **12 departments to choose from:** Powertrain, Chassis & Vehicle Dynamics, E-Mobility, Driver Assistance, Software & Connected Services, Electrical/Electronic, Interior, Body, Product Integration, Manufacturing & Quality, Purchasing & Cost Controlling, and Product Marketing & Sales.
- **Better suggestions:** every requirement in the demo vehicles now gets a specific department; none fall back to "Product Integration". Drivetrain goes to Powertrain, Braking to Chassis, rattles to Quality, value for money to Sales.
- **A draft per department:** each one asks that department's own question. Powertrain is asked about "drivetrain hardware and calibration effort", Purchasing about "cost, sourcing and supplier implications".
- **Your edits are protected:** if you've already changed the draft (by hand or via "Create email from notes"), switching department asks before replacing it.
- **What else follows the switch:** the saved stakeholder email updates per department, the hint shows the original suggestion ("Rerouted by the PM. Suggested department: Powertrain Engineering."), and the reroute is logged in the activity history.

**Two fixes along the way:**
- **Hidden space:** "ground clearance" contains an invisible non-breaking space in the source data, which blocked every rule. Text is now cleaned before matching, for both departments and domains.
- **PDF priority:** the PM and Technical PDFs printed the timeline-fit score as "Priority", the same bug I fixed on the cards earlier.

**Files:** `public/engine.js`, `public/app.js`, `public/readable.css`, `test/engine.test.mjs`.

content.text:
Here's how the knowledge base is built today. I haven't changed anything; I'm waiting for your go-ahead.

## Current knowledge base (`data/`)

| Your category | What exists today | File | How it affects the ranking |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Customer reviews** | 13,771 feedback rows from the 1, 5 and 7 Series. Each has vehicle, market, feedback type (Likes / Difficult to use / Wants / Defect), text, feature category and a quality rating. | `evidence.json` | **Customer demand.** Unique customers per feature, after removing duplicates and low-quality rows. This is the "Customer demand" part of the score. |
| **Market data** | 1,003 customer-study rows (2025 studies for China/EU and the US) and 12 sales-volume rows (2024 / 2025 / 2030). | `context.json` (`studies`, `sales`) | **Market evidence.** Study topics are matched to features by name. Sales add a flat bonus for the vehicle/market. |
| | 132 competitor signals: competitor complaints, competitor equipment, industry studies (Mercedes, Audi, Lexus, Genesis, Cadillac) | `context.json` (`competitors`) | **Market evidence**, matched to a feature. |
| | 13 competitor prices | `context.json` (`competitorPrices`) | Loaded but **not used** in the ranking. |
| **Memory from past cycles** | 1 example decision, labelled "Team-authored demo history" | `historical-decisions.json` | **+5 points** if a new requirement matches a feature from a past decision. |
| | Your own approvals and rejections in the app (124 events so far, mixed with navigation logs) | `decision-events.ndjson` | **Shown in Decision Memory only.** Your real decisions don't yet feed back into the next ranking. |
| **Global trends** | **Nothing.** There's an empty slot for web signals, and the server has a web-research API, but the app never calls it. | (`context.external`, empty) | No effect today. |
| *(sources)* | The 9 original files: 3 feedback workbooks, customer studies, sales, competitor workbook, 3 option-list PDFs | `sources/` | Citations link to these. PDF text isn't read. |

**How the score is built:** customer demand, plus timeline fit (from your months / team / deadline settings), plus market evidence (studies up to 65 points, competitors up to 35, web up to 20, sales +10, capped at 100), plus the memory bonus.

## Proposed next step (for your approval)

An **"Add your own evidence"** panel on the setup page:
1. **Choose the type:** Customer feedback · Market data · Global trend · Past decision.
2. **Vehicle and market** default to the current selection.
3. **Weight 1–10.**
4. **Add the data:** paste text or upload a CSV, with a downloadable template per type.
5. **Preview and check** the rows before they're added.

Each type would go into the existing structure, so ranking, citations and Decision Memory work without being rebuilt:
- **Customer feedback** joins the reviews and counts toward customer demand.
- **Market data** and **global trends** add to market evidence. Trends finally fill the empty web slot.
- **Past decisions** become Decision Memory entries and give the memory bonus.

Every uploaded row is cited as **"PM upload · file · row N"**, clearly marked as user-supplied and never mixed up with BMW data.

**Three decisions before I build:**
1. **Storage:**
   - **(a) On the server** in a new `data/uploads.json`: survives restarts and everyone on the same server sees it. *(Recommended.)*
   - **(b) In the browser only:** private, but lost if the browser data is cleared.
2. **What the weight does:**
   - **(a) Scales that upload's contribution:** 5 = normal, 10 = double, 1 = a fifth. *(Recommended.)*
   - **(b) Only a label**, shown with the evidence.
3. **Which feature a row belongs to:**
   - **(a) Auto-match to existing feature names, with a dropdown to correct it in the preview.** *(Recommended.)*
   - **(b) A required "feature" column in the CSV.**

A related small gap: your own approvals and rejections could also feed back into the memory bonus for future runs. Want that included too?

content.text:
The setup page now has a new section, **"02 / Your evidence – Add your own evidence."**, with your three choices built in: saved on the server, weight scales the contribution, and features are auto-matched with a dropdown to correct them. All 44 tests pass. I also tested the whole flow in Chrome on a separate test server, then removed the test data and stopped it.

**Restart your server before using it:** stop it (Ctrl+C) and run `npm start` again. The app now needs the new upload API, so the old server will show an "outdated PM server" message.

**How it works**
1. **Choose the type:** Customer feedback, Market data, Global trend or Past decision, each with a short note on what it affects.
2. **Set the weight (1–10):** the hint says what it means, e.g. "8 counts 1.6× as much as BMW data". The section also shows which vehicle and market it applies to (the current selection).
3. **Add the data:** paste one item per line, or upload a CSV by drag-and-drop or browsing. Each type has its own **Download CSV template**. Past decisions need the CSV, because they have several fields.
4. **Preview:** each row gets an automatically matched feature that you can change with the dropdown. Rows without a feature are highlighted and left out. You can remove single rows, then click "Add N rows to the knowledge base".
5. **Manage:** saved uploads are listed underneath and can be removed. After adding or removing, a button offers to regenerate the requirements.

**Effect on the ranking**
- **Customer feedback** adds to customer demand, scaled by the weight. The "N customers raised this" count stays honest: weight changes the score, not the number of customers. The reasoning adds "…, 3 of them from your uploads".
- **Market data and global trends** add to market evidence: about 8 points per row at weight 5, capped at 30. Trends finally fill the empty web slot. The reasoning says e.g. "Also backed by … 1 global trend you added".
- **Past decisions** show up in Decision Memory and give a memory bonus equal to their weight (5 at the default).
- **Citations:** every uploaded row is marked "Your data · file · row N", with its own groups ("Your market data", "Global trends you added"). It never links to the BMW source files.
- **Evidence bar:** shows "N rows from your uploads".

**Two bugs found by the tests and fixed:**
- A quote mark in the middle of a CSV field was swallowed.
- "I wish the car came in more colours" was matched to the feature "Caring Car". Generic words like car, BMW and drive no longer count.

**Files**
- **New:** `src/uploads.mjs` (CSV parser, types and templates, feature matching, validation), `test/uploads.test.mjs` (6 tests).
- **Changed:** `server.mjs` (new upload API), `public/engine.js`, `public/app.js`, `public/index.html`, `public/readable.css`, `public/select.js` (dropdown lists are now built only when opened, so a preview with hundreds of rows stays fast).

**Notes**
- Uploads are saved to `data/uploads.json`, created on the first upload. It isn't gitignored, so commit it if the team should share uploads, or tell me to ignore it.
- You didn't answer one earlier question: should your own approvals and rejections in the app also feed the memory bonus? That's not included yet.

# Pitch website with a live demo: how the NeuroSpace deck was built, and what to do better

A write-up of `MNH26SSA/pitch/index.html` (Neuromorphic Hackathon 2026): the stack, the design system, the
animation techniques, the live-demo integration, how it was verified, and every mistake that cost time.
Use it as the starting brief for the next project.

---

## 1. Architecture at a glance

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| `pitch/index.html` | One self-contained HTML file (~1,700 lines): all CSS in one `<style>`, all slides as `<section>`s, all JS at the bottom. No build step, opens by double-click. |
| Slide engine | **Reveal.js 5.1** from the jsDelivr CDN, plus its **Notes** plugin (press `S` for speaker view with timer). |
| Font | **JetBrains Mono** (400–800) from Google Fonts. |
| Live demo | A **Streamlit** dashboard (`streamlit_app.py`) running at `http://localhost:8501`, shown inside the deck as a full-screen interactive background iframe on one slide. |
| Media | Two looping MP4s and PNG frames in `pitch/assets/`, team photos in `../assets/team/`. |
| Script | `SCRIPT.md` (who says what, per click), `SOURCES.md` (a source for every number), speaker notes inside each slide. |
| Design brief | `PRODUCT.md` (users, purpose, principles) + `DESIGN.md` (tokens) at the project root, written before the UI. |

All three changes are in. I ran the full demo in Chrome on a separate test server: uploaded all four files, generated, and checked the cards. All 45 tests pass. Nothing is committed or pushed yet; say the word and I'll push.

**1. Generate button moved:** the setup page now runs in order: **01 Product context → 02 Your evidence (optional) → 03 Generate**. Step 3 restates what will be generated ("BMW 5 Series · United States · 18 months · 12 people · deadline 8/10 · Includes 18 rows of your evidence"), then the button.

| File | Content |

| `1-customer-feedback.csv` | 8 comments about the glass roof, wireless charging and seats. Three have an empty feature column, so the preview shows auto-matching. |

- **Seats:** to #1 in Interior & Comfort.

- "5 customer comments you added (weight 8/10): +1 point of customer demand"
- "2 market data rows and 2 global trends you added: +4 points of market evidence"

- **Rejected past decisions no longer add points.** Before, any uploaded past decision added its weight, even a rejection. Now only approved ones count.

content.text:
The walkthrough is ready at **`walkthrough/index.html`**: one 2.8 MB file that opens in Chrome with no server, no internet and no OpenAI calls. Every screen is a real screenshot of the app. I clicked through all 22 steps at 1440×900 and 1920×1080 with real mouse clicks: no errors, no network requests.

**Flow (follows your "final final slide audio" transcript):**
1. **Intro.**
2. **Demo 1 (9 steps):**
   - set the upfront requirements;
   - upload `1-customer-feedback.csv`, check the preview, add the rows;
   - generate;
   - in Interior & Comfort, open the reasoning of **Seating comfort (#2, 60 points, no past decisions)**;
   - **Move up**, then approve with the reason: *"seat complaints and defects are a real pain point on long US drives, while the audio settings mostly need clearer controls."*
3. **"That was the brief. And what every team built."** with the four steps of the brief.
4. **The quote** appears word by word: *"When I join a project during a handover, I have zero context on what was decided before, or why. I'd love to see the project's past decisions and the reasons behind them."* — Former Product Manager, Vodafone (quoted with his consent).
5. **Demo 2 (8 steps):**
   - a new PM opens the Project Diary and generates the **Onboarding** storyline (real output, zoomed in);
   - enters their own constraints (24 months, 8 people, deadline 5/10) and generates again;
   - Seating comfort now leads, tagged **"Past decision"**;
   - its reasoning zooms into the **Decision Memory** section: the previous PM's reason and **+5 points**. Without those points it would tie for #1 (56 vs 56).
6. **Close:** "Vehicle projects run for years. PMs change. Decisions shouldn't get lost." with Decision memory, Onboarding and Handover. Last line: "We don't replace product managers. We give them the memory of everyone who came before."

**Interaction:**
- **Advancing:** click the pulsing blue box (it's labelled with the action, e.g. "Approve requirement"), or press → / Space; ← goes back.
- **Navigation:** the chapter names at the top jump between sections; F toggles full screen.
- **Animations:** screenshots crossfade, the view zooms into the reasoning, and a cursor glides to each next click.

**App changes this needed (also live in the app now):**
- **Decision Memory feeds reasoning and ranking.** Approvals and rejections recorded in the app, the team's demo history and uploaded past decisions now appear as a "Decision Memory" section. Approved ones add 5 points (uploads add their own weight); rejected ones add no points and are flagged as a caution. Before, your own decisions didn't affect the ranking.
- **Project Diary opens at today:** it used to start at June 2024, which hid all recent activity.

**Things to know:**
- **Decisions in the repo now count.** `data/decision-events.ndjson` holds the team's test approvals (like "approval granted"), and these now give +5 points to those requirements in the live app. Clear it before the pitch if you want clean rankings. I didn't touch it; the walkthrough was captured on a clean copy in `/tmp`.
- **Rebuilding:** `walkthrough/tools/recapture.sh` regenerates the walkthrough after app changes. It calls OpenAI for the wording and the storyline, about 4 minutes in total. Captions are in `walkthrough/tools/build.mjs`.
- **Dates in the screenshots:** they show today (11 Oct 2026), and the storyline is the real AI output from this run.
- **Nothing is committed.** The pitch-deck deletion from earlier is also still uncommitted.

I really like the layout and the design. the only thing that trips me off is that it feels unnatural to switch from one screenshot to another screenshot and I feel like the audience won't have like any coherent walkthrough of the demo. So I need you to either spam screenshots or do a screen recording to also add the scrolling animations and stuff.y coherent walkthrough of the demo. So I need you to either spam screenshots or do a screen recording to also add the scrolling animations and stuff.

Good call. A recording will feel much more natural than jumping between screenshots. Here's the plan:

- **Record the real app:** use Chrome's built-in screen recording while it drives the app, with a visible cursor that glides to each control and clicks, smooth scrolling, and typed text.
- **Cut into clips:** one clip per step, with the long AI waits trimmed out.
- **Same player as before:** clicking the highlighted control plays the next clip, so the audience sees one continuous journey. At the end of each clip the hotspot and zoom appear as they do now.

content.text:
The walkthrough now plays a **screen recording of the real app**, one clip per step, instead of jumping between screenshots. All 25 steps play through, and all 50 app tests pass.

- **What the audience sees:** a cursor gliding to each control and clicking, smooth scrolling, the typed reason, the loading state, and the requirements appearing. The AI waits are trimmed to about 1.4 s, and the whole demo is about 90 seconds of footage.
- **How you drive it:** each clip ends paused on the next control, highlighted with the blue pulsing box. Click it (or press → / Space) and the next clip starts exactly where the last one ended, so it reads as one continuous journey. Pressing → during a clip skips to its end, and ← or a chapter jump shows the end state without replaying.
- **Checked:** I clicked through all 25 steps in headless Chrome with real mouse clicks. Every clip played, every hotspot appeared at the end of its clip, and there were no errors and no network requests (no OpenAI, no CDN).

**Your two additions:**
1. **Competitor sources in demo 1:** after the reasoning, the cursor clicks "View cited sources", the drawer scrolls to the **9 Competitors** (Mercedes E-Class and Audi A6 reports and equipment lists, each with row and original source) and zooms in. Then it closes and continues with Move up.
2. **Score bar split:** **Competitor data** is now its own teal segment in the app's score bar, next to customer demand, timeline fit and market evidence. For example, Drivetrain is now 44 + 32 + 10 + 5 = 91. Demo 2 ends on a new step that scrolls to the bar for Seating comfort: demand 14, timeline 35, market 2, **competitor data 5**, **past decisions 5**, for **61** versus 56 for the next requirement.

**Notes:**
